description: Make a NEW Generalist Gripper version using the Aero Hand servos (Jake said arrow hand). Confirmed upstream firmware README specifies Feetech HLS3606M. Build on latest Base 17 / Gripper 24 v318_generalist_tiny_v2 unless newer lands: recognizable curved lattice fingers, separate geared drive, compact as feasible, actual servo mounting. Preserve old versions. Gear sizes/ratio may change per Jake earlier authorization. Use manufacturer HLS3606M drawing https://www.feetechrc.com/Data/feetechrc/upload/file/20240807/6385862508379674057566108.pdf and vendored Aero Hand CAD/parts to verify exact single/double shaft variant, screw pattern, horn/spline, cable and assembly clearance; do not invent scaled mounting hardware. Nominal body 23x12x27.5mm is not mounting evidence. Reuse actual Aero Hand horn/pulley interface if suitable. Bump only changed part counters, params.json source of truth, export CAD and run geometry/genus/full-stroke hardware clearance checks, publish live preview and comparison render. Identify measured vs assumed fit dimensions and no unproven force rating. No physical motor actuation. Use GPT-6.1 Sol medium.

results.identified_issue: Base 17 uses STS3215 hardware; nominal HLS body dimensions cannot justify scaling that interface. Manufacturer PDF identifies HLS3606M-C001 single output, 25T/4.95 spline, M2.3x5 retaining screw and clearance ear holes. Pinned Aero STEP solids 304/248/61 identify actual single-output servo, purchased 18 mm aluminum plate and cable spool. Reused three original spool attachment holes and M2x4 screws; deep pinion wells leave 2.25 mm grip / 1.75 mm modeled plate engagement. Actual plate threads and head sizes need measurement. Four original-guide M2x6 self-tapping ear screws enter from below into 4.8 mm blind pilots (4.5 mm modeled bite); 0.5 mm slots cover manufacturer/CAD ear-center discrepancy of 0.25 mm. Servo points toward pivots underneath base to fit within inherited width/height. No Gripper bump: both finger meshes, side gears and cap exactly match Base 17. Only Base 18 advances. Full-stroke check: 91 pairs × 121 poses = 11011, no pair exclusions, 0.0001 mm^3 numerical tolerance for submicron seated-plane STL rounding. Deliberate spline/thread engagement omitted from screw probes; full exported motor and plate solids included. Source STEP reports one unresolved reference; raw servo/spool tessellation has seams, repaired by OpenSCAD Manifold import; actual collision-export motor and plate watertight. Provenance, measured/assumed dimensions, CC BY-NC-SA license and limits in README/reference. Cable service corridor assumed, fine-resin web 0.4047 mm, physical fit/pullout/force unproven. Export, genus, geometry, hardware positive controls, live Tune contract, 15 publisher tests and 13 gallery tests passed. Published catalog without application build; screenshot verified using headless Chrome SwiftShader. No motor actuation.
results.summary: Added Base 18 with the Aero Hand servo and unchanged Gripper 24 fingers.
results.detailed_description:
Base 18 uses the single-shaft HLS3606M and its real aluminum spline plate. The new pinion reuses the Aero Hand spool’s three M2 screws; ear screws mount from below. Short pilot slots cover the 0.25 mm drawing/CAD discrepancy.

Gripper 24’s lattice fingers stay unchanged. Depth drops from 62.90 to 46.40 mm with the new cable routing; width and height stay the same. Select Base 18 + Gripper 24 in the preview; CAD and comparison are attached.

Geometry/genus checks, 11,011 stroke clearance checks and 28 gallery/publisher tests pass. Cable clearance is assumed; this remains a fine-resin prototype needing physical fit and strength checks. No force rating or motor actuation.

visual.alt: Base 17 versus Base 18, with unchanged lattice fingers and a shallower servo assembly
